, Claude mentions it once and asks whether to bring the useful fixes into your copy. The steps Claude follows are in [`MY-STYLES.md`](MY-STYLES.md). ### Before you start - A film takes an agent about 30–60 minutes and a fair amount of tokens. - You need Node 20+, ffmpeg 7+ and Python 3.11+ (or [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/)); the agent installs the rest. Ubuntu 24.04 ships ffmpeg 6.1, which is too old: use a [static build](https://johnvansickle.com/ffmpeg/). - Default output 1920×1080, 24 fps; other sizes on request. ### Update or uninstall Update, then restart Claude Code (the library in `~/lemo-opuscar` updates itself on the next film): ```sh claude plugin marketplace update lemolab && claude plugin update lemo-opuscar@lemolab ``` After an update, ask for a film as usual; to make a style your own, see [above](#make-a-style-your-own). Uninstall, then delete `~/lemo-opuscar`: ```sh claude plugin uninstall lemo-opuscar@lemolab ``` Your own styles in `~/lemo-my-styles/` stay through updates and uninstalls; delete that folder yourself if you don't want them. If a step stays stuck, [open an issue](https://github.com/lemomo-ai/lemo-opuscar/issues). ## The styles Click a frame for its `STYLE.md`. ### 🆕 New · 2026-10-29
### Edit & Documentary
### Evidence Films
### Hand-drawn & Painting
### East Asian Traditions
### Print & Printmaking ====SKILL --- name: lemo-opuscar description: Direct and produce a short film made entirely in code, in one of the styles of the Lemo-Opuscar library (e.g. Impasto Oil Painting 油画厚涂, Watercolor Brush 水彩笔刷, Ukiyo-e 浮世绘, Satellite Briefing 卫星简报, Exploded Teardown 产品拆解). Use when the user asks for a video, film, short, promo, explainer or animation (视频、短片、动画、宣传片) in a named style, including explainers built from real material such as satellite imagery, laser scans, CAD files or archive scans (数据解说、科普、产品拆解), and new films cut from real archive footage and documents (剪辑与纪实, e.g. 用档案影像剪一支新闻片); when they want a film about their own topic and haven't chosen a style (help them choose); when they want to change a style into their own, make their own style from a blank page, or use a style they saved (改风格、从空白开始、我的风格); when they start the skill without saying what they want; or when they ask which film styles there are. Not for plain editing, trimming or converting the user's existing video files. --- # Lemo-Opuscar The styles, guides and tools ship with this plugin, in `library/` next to this file. Nothing is downloaded to tell you what to do. 1. **Get the library ready.** Run `sh "/scripts/setup.sh"`. It copies the bundled library to its working folder (default `~/.lemo-opuscar`, so installed packages survive plugin updates) and prints `LIB=` on its last line. 2. **Install the core tools early.** Start `sh "/scripts/setup.sh" deps` right away, in the background if you can: it takes a few minutes the first time. Add `deps voice` or `deps music` later, only if the film needs them (`$LIB/TECHNIQUE.md` §1). Report missing system tools (Node, ffmpeg, Python) in your one round of questions; don't install system software yourself. Packages a style needs (its `STYLE.md` lists them) you install yourself, into the project folder. 3. **Follow the library.** Read `$LIB/AGENTS.md` and do what it says, starting with **Start** (the user's own styles in `~/lemo-my-styles/`; when they started the skill without writing anything, the language question first, then the ways in): finding the style or making their own, the one round of questions, the treatment, production and delivery. What changes in skill mode: | | | |---|---| | Project folder | `/` in the folder the user started from (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens; avoid `#` and `?` in the path). Wherever the guides say `films//`, read this folder | | Running tools | from `$LIB`, with the project's absolute path: `cd "$LIB" && node core/render/still.mjs "" 1.5 3`. `sh tools/setup.sh` and `sh tools/fetch.sh` also run from `$LIB` | | Library files in pages | absolute URLs: `/core/lib.js`, `/node_modules/three/…` (the project is served at `/@film/`) | | Library files in scripts and `build.sh` | `$LIB/…`, with `LIB=` at the top of `build.sh`; never `../..` | | Demo films | not in this edition: no `demo/` source and no `poster.jpg`. Each style's `DEMO.md` (how its demo was made) is there; read it only after your `TREATMENT.md` is written, as the guides say. An Edit & Documentary style needs its material before the treatment: find and log it yourself, as its `STYLE.md` describes (the `demo/tools/` it names aren't in this edition). The films are on the gallery, https://lemomo-ai.github.io/lemo-opuscar/, if the user wants to watch one | | Chinese narration | Kokoro's Chinese voices (offline) by default. edge-tts (`core/tts/tts_zh.py`) sounds better but sends the narration text to Microsoft's speech service: offer it in your one round of questions and use it only if the user agrees | | Big downloads | only what the film needs, from the sources `$LIB/TECHNIQUE.md` §1 lists (npm, PyPI, Playwright's browser, this library's GitHub Releases, Hugging Face for the speech check). Name them in your one round of questions the first time | Deliver what `$LIB/DIRECTOR.md` §11 lists, in the project folder, and tell the user where it is. ====PKG { "name": "lemo-opuscar", "version": "0.1.0", "private": true, "type": "module", "description": "Film styles for coding agents: each style ships a prompt and a demo film made entirely in code, on a shared toolkit.", "engines": { "node": ">=20" }, "license": "MIT", "dependencies": { "playwright-core": "^1.63.0", "three": "^0.170.0" } }
